payout_quote: IRS: 'If you e-filed your return, after 24 hours, you can go to irs.gov/refund to check on its status using our Where's My Refund? tool.' This finds YOUR OWN tax refund money — overpaid tax the government owes back to you — if it is delayed, lost, or undelivered; it never promises anyone is owed any.
timing: Refund status generally available within 24 hours of e-file acknowledgment (4 weeks for paper). Typical payout: about 21 days for e-filed direct-deposit refunds. Lost/stolen check trace via Form 3911: the Bureau of the Fiscal Service review can take up to six weeks.
biggest_catch: This only tracks a refund from a return you already filed — it cannot create money or find refunds you never claimed by filing. The IRS cautions: 'don't rely on receiving a refund by a certain date,' and returns claiming the Earned Income Tax Credit or Additional Child Tax Credit are legally held until mid-February.
eligibility: Anyone who filed a federal tax return expecting a refund. Where's My Refund needs your SSN, filing status, and the exact refund amount from the return.
steps: Go to https://www.irs.gov/refund and use Where's My Refund? with your SSN, filing status, and exact refund amount (or the IRS2Go mobile app).
If it shows the refund was sent but you never got it: if you moved, file Form 8822 to update your address with the IRS.

If the check is lost or was never delivered, initiate a refund trace — in Where's My Refund, via the automated line 800-829-1954, or by filing Form 3911 (Taxpayer Statement Regarding Refund); married-filing-jointly filers must use the form or call 800-829-1040.

If the check was cashed by someone else, the Bureau of the Fiscal Service sends a claim package (up to six weeks for review); if it was never cashed, a replacement is issued once the original is canceled.
catches: Only works for refunds on returns you actually filed — no return, no refund to find.
Do not rely on a specific date; some returns need additional review and take longer.
EITC/Additional Child Tax Credit refunds are held by law until mid-February.
Paper tax refund checks are being phased out (since Sept 30, 2025) — direct deposit is the default path.
The IRS will never call/text/email demanding payment or personal info about your refund — those are scams.
notes: Verified 2026-09-22/23 against official irs.gov pages (refund FAQs, Where's My Refund guidance, IR-2025-94 on the paper-check phaseout, IR-2026-44). App links: the official IRS2Go app exists on both stores — named without a guessed store URL, per the no-guess rule. In-app, frame strictly as tracking your own already-filed refund, and include the IRS-scam warning. c1.evidence: IRS — the Internal Revenue Service, the US federal tax agency — operates Where's My Refund and the refund-trace process.

c2.evidence: Official irs.gov pages describe Where's My Refund (SSN + filing status + exact amount) and the lost-check trace via Form 3911 / 800-829-1954.

c3.evidence: Checking and tracing a refund are free; no fee anywhere in the official process.

c4.evidence: Official IRS pages state timing plainly: 24h for e-file status, ~21 days typical, up to six weeks for BFS review of a cashed-check claim.

s2.note: Free; IRS-scam impersonation is the cost risk, not a fee.

s3.note: ~21 days typical for e-filed direct deposit; up to six weeks for a lost-check trace review.

s4.note: No weasel words — the IRS is explicit that dates are not guaranteed.
